solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fight in yard

definitions.meaning: to box or fight, often in practice
on a sailing ship a yard is a ..., the pole a sail hangs from

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: a boxing verb for sparring, and the nautical noun for a pole on a mast.

clue.text: A patron's inn damaged equally on both sides

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub-goer's local has been vandalised, apparently by both factions alike.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'patron's' is a real letter of the fodder: A PATRONS INN gives exactly eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being non-aligned with any faction means favouring each side equally, without bias.

clue.text: Bad-tempered taxi driver carrying Queen

indicators.note: the cab driver is carrying, so holding inside, the royal letter

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A grumpy cabbie has a royal passenger in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone crabby is irritable and cross, like a bad-tempered crab.

clue.text: Stub blunt weapon under bar

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece placed under another is written after it

parts.note: a counter is a bar, as in a shop or pub
a foil is a fencing sword with a blunted tip

explanation.surface: A cosh is hidden beneath the pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfoil is the stub of a cheque or ticket kept as a record.

clue.text: Druggie did act suspiciously

indicators.note: behaving suspiciously means acting oddly, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug user behaved in a way that aroused suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a druggie is a slang word for someone dependent on narcotics.

clue.text: Top Gear to such as Father Ted, best art I broadcast

definitions.text: Top Gear to such as Father Ted

indicators.note: broadcast can mean scattered widely, so these letters are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV-themed clue linking the motoring show Top Gear and the sitcom Father Ted, with the best art on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Gear' and 'Father Ted' pose as TV programme titles; really 'top gear' is headwear and Father Ted is just an example of a priest. Father Ted was a sitcom about Irish priests.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Catholic clergy, literally top gear for priests.

clue.text: Thoroughly search company doctor

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A firm's medic is going through everything with a fine-tooth approach.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it painstakingly, as if drawing a comb through it.

clue.text: Car's beginning to shake — it's clapped-out

indicators.note: the start of the word 'Car' supplies its first letter only

parts.note: to rock is to shake or sway

explanation.surface: An old banger starts rattling the moment you set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car' tempts as the definition, but only its first letter is used; the definition is the closing phrase, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock is a worn-out old vehicle or person, something decrepit and broken down.

clue.text: Fruit gives person energy

parts.note: a man is a person
go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Eating fruit gives a person a burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Picture in post office is very exciting

indicators.note: the exciting word sits in the post office abbreviation

parts.note: hot can mean very exciting, as in a hot story

explanation.surface: A picture displayed in the post office is causing a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a photo is a photographic picture.

clue.text: Foreign articles wore down resistance group

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article
DER is a German definite article
ground is the past tense of grind, so wore down

explanation.surface: Overseas newspaper pieces gradually eroded a rebel movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A wartime resistance movement operating in secret is called the underground.

clue.text: Last words on northern city

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, are the final words on a gravestone

explanation.surface: The final remarks about a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Credit to English concealing strategic move in game

indicators.note: the credit-to-English string conceals, so holds inside, the move

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
a tack is a course of action or approach

explanation.surface: Giving English the credit hides a clever ploy in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is the American name for noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American name for noughts and crosses, a simple pencil-and-paper game.

clue.text: Those wanting to save money caught fish put in piles

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the fish is put inside the caught-plus-piles string

parts.note: heaps are piles
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Anglers land fish and stack them in heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapskates are stingy people reluctant to spend, so they are always saving money.

clue.text: Discussing business — there's pounds to be had in money received on short flight

indicators.note: the pounds are to be found inside the takings

parts.note: takings are the money a shop or business receives
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds sterling
a hop is a short plane journey

explanation.surface: Talking about work: there's cash in the till from a brief airline route.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to talk shop is to discuss one's work or business, especially socially.

clue.text: Call in the Spanish material that's glossy

indicators.note: the call word sits inside the Spanish article

parts.note: EL is Spanish for the
to name someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Ringing up about some shiny Spanish fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glassy coating or gloss paint, a material with a hard shiny finish.

clue.text: Cancer perhaps — subject is about right

indicators.note: the subject goes about, so around, the letter for right

parts.note: a topic is a subject

explanation.surface: Discussing a disease is fair enough as a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancer' looks like the illness, but it is the Tropic of Cancer, a line of latitude; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Cancer is one of the two tropics, so Cancer is an example of a tropic.

clue.text: Sharp reply regarding wrong

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A cutting answer about an injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a retort is a quick, sharp or witty answer.

clue.text: Bush gets everyone around Middle East detained by his secret service

indicators.note: that group is held inside the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the American secret service, his if the president Bush is the subject

indicators.note: everyone goes around the Middle East letters

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: President Bush has everyone across the Middle East locked up by his spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' reads as the former US president, which makes the CIA his own service; really it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is an evergreen flowering shrub, so it is a kind of bush.

clue.text: Carrier for young fish I catch

parts.note: bass is a fish
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: An angler announcing a fish they have landed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded basket or pram used to carry a baby.

clue.text: Country ended test

parts.note: something past is over or ended
an oral is a spoken test or exam

explanation.surface: A nation's examination is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation noun, but it is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural country life, an adjective for the countryside.

clue.text: Goblin sets heart of fairies in bad feeling

indicators.note: the middle letter goes in the bad-feeling word

parts.note: spite is malice or ill will

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A goblin puts malice into the hearts of fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or goblin-like supernatural creature.

clue.text: Remove sleazy venue's permit finally

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar, here with its possessive S

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word permit

explanation.surface: Take away the licence from the disreputable club.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip off or take away, as of possessions or clothing.

clue.text: One often found in church, leader of Catholics, tackled sin vigorously

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
done vigorously these letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: In church, the head of the Catholics took on sin with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlesticks hold candles on altars, so they are commonly seen in churches.

clue.text: A prison in commotion

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail is in uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means in a state of excitement or movement, all stirred up.

clue.text: Channel contains a gold coin

indicators.note: the channel word contains the single letter

parts.note: a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: A waterway holds a golden piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin used across Europe, especially in Venice.

clue.text: A recurring question for ancient storyteller

indicators.note: recurring means turning back, so the question word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pose is to put a question

explanation.surface: A question keeps coming up for an old narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Settles French country

definitions.meaning: settles a bill means hands over the money owed
the French word for a country or land

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an English verb for settling accounts, and the French noun for a nation.

clue.text: Leggy creature to remain with religious group

parts.note: to stick in is to stay put
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A long-legged animal stays with a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick insect has a long thin body and very long legs, so it is a leggy creature.

clue.text: Furniture's finish with thin dark wood

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

parts.note: bony means skinny or thin

explanation.surface: A furniture maker finishes a slim piece in dark timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a very dark, hard wood from tropical trees.

clue.text: King George has the very thing — determination

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A monarch has exactly what he needs: resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage and resolve, firmness of character.

clue.text: Facts and figures about university show prestige

indicators.note: the statistics wrap around the university letter

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are facts and figures

explanation.surface: Data on a university reveal how highly it is regarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: status is standing or prestige in society.
